episode_title: And then there was that little PHP vulnerability

real_qa.q: What is the PHP vulnerability affecting 70 percent of the internet and which platforms are impacted?
real_qa.r: 70 percent of the internet is vulnerable to this PHP vulnerability, including any sites that run on WordPress and e-commerce sites like Magento. These are age old vulnerabilities that have just been sitting there. The vulnerability is so simple to identify that it has impacted critical infrastructure and government sites.
real_qa.requete: PHP vulnerability 70 percent internet WordPress Magento

real_qa.q: Why did Chainguard violate the coordinated disclosure embargo for the PHP vulnerability?
real_qa.r: Chainguard released the PHP vulnerability fix six hours before the coordinated disclosure was supposed to go out, claiming they were seeing it being exploited in the wild and had to protect their customers. The CEO and founder of Chainguard posted on LinkedIn explaining they had to do it because it was the right thing to do. However, PHP called them out on their blog, noting that breaking the embargo gave bad actors time to create exploits before patches were available.
real_qa.requete: Chainguard PHP vulnerability coordinated disclosure embargo breach

real_qa.q: What alternative approach to vulnerability prioritization can help organizations manage large backlogs?
real_qa.r: Organizations should move away from CVSS scoring to a more risk-based approach, looking at whether vulnerabilities have a known exploit, the probability of that exploit being utilized, and whether it impacts customers or internal data. This prevents throwing 70,000 vulnerabilities at engineers who are already too busy pushing code, allowing teams to focus on what actually matters.
real_qa.requete: risk-based vulnerability management CVSS scoring alternative

real_qa.q: How has the publication rate of CVEs changed and what impact does this have on organizations?
real_qa.r: Published CVEs have doubled this year, and this does not even count the amount of vulnerabilities that have not been published or disclosed. Combined with AI making it easier to discover and exploit additional vulnerabilities, this creates a compounding effect where vulnerability management becomes increasingly difficult.

real_qa.q: What other vulnerabilities besides PHP were disclosed during this period?
real_qa.r: Light LLM and Node.js both released vulnerabilities this week, though the PHP vulnerability overshadowed all of them. The timing of multiple critical disclosures in the same week created significant strain on security teams.

guest.bio_context: Kendra has experience in both defensive and offensive security perspectives. She has worked in organizations implementing risk-based vulnerability management approaches, moving away from CVSS scoring to prioritize vulnerabilities based on known exploits and customer impact. She is currently unemployed at the time of this recording.

real_quote: Vulnerability management has always been a huge problem in the security industry. It's a known problem, right? And there's an expectation that organizations are going to have a huge backlog of vulnerabilities.
